The Jade Chapters describes the Biao horse as "fierce and brave," known for its speed and the small, speckled spots marking its coat. Among the Southwestern Ponies, those with this distinct red-dappled pattern are called Chibiao.
Legends from the Huayang Chorography tell of a divine steed that once rose from Dianchi Lake. Its offspring, known as "Dianchi Foals," were said to travel five hundred li a day. Later, during the Tang and Song dynasties, texts like the Book of the Man and the New Book of Tang praised the swift, high-tailed horses bred on the lush grasslands of the region, famed as "Yuetan Steeds." These Dian Horses, named for their origin near Dianchi Lake, are also known as Southwestern Ponies.
Small in stature, they have fine limbs, a short neck, a broad forehead, and firm, compact hooves. Prized for their endurance, they are suited for riding, pulling, and carrying loads, making them the most common breed in the southwest.

To my young brother, 
   If you're reading this, then you know what has happened, and you likely have doubts in your heart. I thought about this for a long time and made up my mind. For many years, I blamed the death of Father Li on my adoptive father. Recently, through the master, I discovered that I had been harboring my hatred for the wrong person. Father Li was killed by a single phrase from the government: "When there are no more birds, the bow becomes useless." I had been in the wrong for many years and assisted the culprit. The kindness of my adoptive father and the revenge for Father Li... I bear both on my shoulders. 
   Only by destroying the ship can I put an end to this. Now I can go see Father Li. 
   Please fulfill my wish by stopping the hatred and not coming with me. Take care of yourself, and put on more clothes when the weather gets cold.
